text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] GPU pool capacity alarm: inference-queue length > 500 for 6m. paging on-call. priority: P1. Incident created INC-1298. :rotating_light:

oncall-anya: I got paged, joining. queue growth visible in the console, customers reporting timeouts. pinging SRE. :pager:

sre-aaron: on it. first quick check: kubernetes job queue shows steady enqueue, workers not scaling. suspect autoscaler / nodegroup attach issue.

infra-maya: ASG for gpu-nodegroup is at Desired=0 Min=0 Max=6 and currently at 6 (maxed). recent scale-up attempts failed with AttachInstanceProfile errors.

infra-maya: pasted error from AWS API: ```
Failed to attach IAM instance profile for instance i-0abc123: AccessDenied: iam:PassRole
status code: 403, request id: 7f1a-xxxx
```

ops-lee: that looks like instance profile / role not allowed to be assumed by the autoscaler. Could be a recent policy drift or a launch template change.

sre-aaron: can someone share recent deploys that touched nodegroup/launch template? @product-nina?

product-nina: no infra deploy from product in last 48h. infra-maya, any terraform plan/applied recently?

infra-maya: There was a rollout of a new launch template version ~2h ago (LT v7 -> v8) to toggle kernel param for GPU scheduling. I see the new launch template omits the instance-profile attribute by mistake. Oops.

oncall-anya: that would explain AttachInstanceProfile failure. New instances are being launched without instance-profile, so they can't attach roles that allow kubelet/kubelet-bootstrap, plus eks node join fails.

ml-chris: consequence is pods waiting for GPU nodes remain queued => substantial customer impact for heavy model infer requests. We already see SLO violations.

support-julia: Support: we have 6 enterprise customers with degraded throughput (higher latency, some 502s). I'll notify account leads after this thread.

sre-aaron: immediate mitigation plan: 1) set ASG Desired down to 4 to avoid more failing launches (reduce churn) 2) manually launch a compatible instance with correct instance-profile from previous LT (v7) and add to cluster 3) revert LT to v7 or patch LT to include instance-profile 4) open emergency infra change to raise ASG Max to 8 and ensure instance-profile presence.

infra-maya: doing manual launch now using AMI+LT v7 config and instance-profile=redwood-node-role. launching 2 warm nodes.

ops-lee: while that's in flight, we should also route non-critical jobs to CPU fallback pool. ml-chris can we deprioritize batch infer for now?

ml-chris: yes we can mark some queues as lower priority and route to cpu-pool. Doing a rollout of routing rule: route model-heavy requests for non-enterprise customers to cpu-backfill.

sre-aaron: check kube: ```kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep NotReady``` shows a couple of Pending nodes with reason 'InstanceNotFound' and several NotReady with kubelet errors. kubectl describe node i-0abc shows: 

```
Events:
  Warning  FailedToRegister  2m (x8 over 10m)  kubelet, ip-10-0-1-23 
  Error: node "ip-10-0-1-23" couldn't be registered: AccessDenied: iam:PassRole
```

sre-aaron: so new nodes are stuck during init, they can't assume role to write tags/SSM and kubelet bootstrap fails.

infra-maya: I patched launch template to include InstanceProfile. Also pushed a temporary policy exception to allow iam:PassRole for AutoScalingServiceRole -> node role. Will monitor.

incident-bot: Action logged: LT patched, instance-profile restored. Notifying oncall.

oncall-anya: rolling up: attempting scale action now to bring ASG back to expected: setting Desired=6, Max=8.

infra-maya: scaling up.. AWS shows 2 instances launched and now one reached InService. kubelet registered node ip-10-0-2-45, taints: gpu=true:NoSchedule set (expected).

sre-aaron: verifying pods: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending` -> queue consumer pods are now scheduling onto the new node. dequeue rate improving.

support-julia: customer update: sent short note to affected customers, apology + we're restoring capacity, ETA 15-30m.

ops-lee: quick note: we saw another failure mode on older nodes where launch template added a taint key gpu=true but nodegroup autoscaling configuration expects taint key gpu:NoSchedule, mismatch caused kube-scheduler to avoid nodes. double-checking taint/key semantics.

sre-aaron: good catch. I saw some pods with tolerations gpu:NoSchedule but key mismatch prevented scheduling earlier. fixing toleration on queue consumers to tolerate both `gpu=true:NoSchedule` and `gpu:NoSchedule` variants as a short-term fix.

ml-chris: metrics: queue length peaked at ~1.2k, token throughput dropped ~60%, 90th latency spiked to 18s for enterprise customers. We'll need to tie these to postmortem.

oncall-anya: status: intake stabilized, new nodes joined, queue draining visible, customer impact decreasing. still watching for ~20m.

product-nina: any root cause TL;DR for support and CSMs?

sre-aaron: TL;DR: recent launch template rollout accidentally dropped the instance-profile attribute which resulted in new instances being launched without the node role; autoscaler launches failed to attach the role (AccessDenied), new nodes couldn't bootstrap, cluster ran out of usable GPU capacity and queue grew. Contrib factors: taint key mismatch made scheduling slower.

support-julia: noted. I'll send updated customer message with TL;DR and next steps.

ops-lee: temporary remediation checklist posted to #eng-ops: revert LT -> v7, verify instance-profile, increase ASG max, patch tolerations, and add CI check to prevent LT missing instance-profile in future.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1298 transition status -> mitigation in progress. Severity remains P1 until queue < 50 and latency back within SLOs.

oncall-anya: handing off to SRE on-call for 03:00 shift, tagging @sre-aaron. Aaron, please take lead for next 2 hours and coordinate postmortem.

sre-aaron: taking lead. will run full blast radius analysis, collect kube logs, ASG events, and IAM change history. Please add any console artifacts to INC-1298 ticket.

product-nina: request postmortem with timeline and action items (CI for LT validation, automated compare of LT instance-profile vs nodegroup config, extra canary for LT changes).

ml-chris: also suggest we enable a soft-fallback route at the API layer to gracefully divert to dedicated/reserved capacity if GPU pool is degraded. This would reduce customer-facing errors next time.

support-julia: logging outreach done. Will keep account reps updated.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1298: mitigation update recorded. Current queue=87, token throughput 85% of baseline, estimated full recovery 12m.

oncall-anya: closing my shift, leaving context in ticket. thanks team. :thumbsup:

sre-aaron: will remain on for handover, will start postmortem doc after stabilization. please add me to any follow-ups.

support-julia: follow-up note: we observed 6 customers impacted, highest impact was one enterprise with > 30% request failures during peak. Tracking for SLA credits if required.

product-nina: please include business impact table in postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1298 marked: mitigation stable -> moving to monitoring. Create follow-up in #postmortems when ready.

sre-aaron: post-incident next steps (short): 1) revert LT and confirm via CI 2) add LT instance-profile presence check in terraform plan gate 3) patch autoscaler role policy checks for clearer error messages 4) add canary scaling test every deploy to LT 5) fix toleration mismatch and add e2e scheduling test.

support-julia: ack, prepping comms for account recovery.

ops-lee: leaving final reminder: link ASG events + CloudTrail IAM events to ticket for root cause.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1298 closed for active mitigation. File for postmortem: INC-1298-PM.

(reacts: everyone :white_check_mark:)
